items.question: How many days per week can an employee work remotely at Voltaria?
items.answer:
Eligible employees at Voltaria may work remotely **up to 3 days per week** [1].

Related conditions:
- Each team sets one **anchor day** per week when everyone is on site [1].
- Core collaboration hours are **10:00 to 16:00 (Paris time)**, and meetings should be scheduled within this window [1].
- Remote days must be declared in PeopleHub by Friday for the following week [1].
- Unused remote days cannot be carried over to the next week [1].
items.correctness_rationale: The answer gets the main figure right (up to 3 days per week) and mentions the team anchor day. It leaves out a key condition from the reference: remote work is only allowed once the probation period is completed. It only says "eligible employees" without explaining what makes someone eligible.
unsupported_claims: The remote work policy belongs to a company called Voltaria.

items.question: What is the monthly home-office allowance and who is entitled to it?
items.answer:
The home-office allowance is **€45 per month**, paid with the monthly salary, for employees who work remotely **at least two days per week** [1].

To work remotely at all, an employee must be eligible under the Remote Work Policy:
- **Probation completed:** eligibility starts after the probation period, which is three months for most roles [2].
- **Excluded roles:** roles that require physical presence, such as field technicians and the Lyon control-room operators, are not eligible [2].
- **Interns and apprentices:** they may work remotely only one day per week, with their tutor's agreement [2]. That is below the two-day threshold for the allowance [1][2].

Related equipment benefits:
- Eligible employees receive a laptop, a 27-inch monitor and a headset [1].
- An ergonomic chair can be reimbursed up to **€250 once every five years**, on presentation of an invoice through Expensio [1].
items.correctness_rationale: The answer gives €45 per month, paid with the salary, for employees working remotely at least two days per week, which matches every key fact in the reference. The extra details don't contradict it.

items.question: Can I work remotely from Canada for two weeks?
items.answer:
**No.** Under the Remote Work Policy, working from outside the EU/EEA and Switzerland is not allowed for tax, employment-law and data-security reasons, so Canada is not permitted [1].

What the policy does allow:
- **Where:** another country of the EU/EEA or Switzerland [1].
- **How long:** up to **20 working days per calendar year**. A two-week stay would fit within that limit [1].
- **Approval:** your manager and HR must approve the request in PeopleHub at least 10 business days in advance [1].
- **Security:** you must use the corporate VPN, never work on Restricted data in public places, and lock your screen whenever you leave your device [2].
items.correctness_rationale: The answer correctly says no and explains that work from outside the EU/EEA and Switzerland is not allowed. It also includes every other key fact from the reference: the 20-working-day annual limit and approval 10 business days in advance. The extra security details don't contradict the reference.

items.question: How long is the paid parental leave for the second parent?
items.answer:
The second parent gets **6 weeks of leave at full salary**, to be taken within the first six months after the birth or adoption [1].

On returning from leave, parents may also work part-time (80%) for up to six months at a 90% salary [1].
items.correctness_rationale: The answer gives every key fact in the reference: 6 weeks at full salary, to be taken within the first six months after the birth or adoption. The extra detail about part-time work doesn't contradict the reference.

items.question: How many unused paid leave days can I carry over to next year, and until when can I use them?
items.answer:
You can carry over **up to 5 days** of unused paid leave to the following year, and you must use them **before 31 March** [1].

- **Deadline exception:** Carried-over days are lost after 31 March unless you couldn't take them because of sick leave or parental leave [1].
- **RTT days:** If you're on the "forfait jours" arrangement, your **10 RTT days** per year cannot be carried over [2].
items.correctness_rationale: The answer gives both key facts from the reference: up to 5 days can be carried over, and they must be used before 31 March. The extra details do not contradict the reference.

items.answer:
The maximum hotel rate for a business trip to Paris is **€180 per night**, breakfast included [1].

- Exceptions, such as trade fairs or events, must be pre-approved by the manager in Navette [1].

items.question: Above which amount does an expense report need approval from a finance controller?
items.answer:
Expense reports above **€2,000** require approval from a finance controller, in addition to manager approval [1].

- Above **€2,000**: finance controller approval is also required [1].

items.question: Can I use a public generative AI chatbot to summarise a confidential supplier contract?
items.answer:
**No.** A supplier contract is Confidential information, and public generative-AI tools may only be used with **Public** information [1][2].

- **Classification:** Contracts are explicitly listed as **Confidential** ("sensitive business information") [2].
- **Approved alternative:** Confidential information may only be processed in the approved **Voltaria AI Workspace**. It keeps data within the EU and does not use it for model training [1].
- **Consequences:** Breaches of the Information Security Policy may lead to disciplinary action [3].

You can use the Voltaria AI Workspace to summarise the contract instead.
items.correctness_rationale: The answer says no, states that public tools may only be used with Public information, and says Confidential information may only be processed in the Voltaria AI Workspace. That covers every key fact in the reference, and the extra details don't contradict it.

items.question: How quickly must a suspected phishing incident be reported, and to whom?
items.answer:
A suspected phishing incident must be reported to the **Security Operations Centre within 1 hour** [1].

You can report it in either of two ways [1]:
- **Email:** security@voltaria.example
- **Phone:** internal extension **4444**, available 24/7

The same rule applies to any suspected security incident, including malware, a data leak or a lost device [1].
items.correctness_rationale: The answer has every key fact from the reference: report within 1 hour, to the Security Operations Centre, by email at security@voltaria.example or on extension 4444, available 24/7. Nothing in it contradicts the reference.

items.question: A supplier offered me a bottle of wine worth EUR 120. What should I do?
items.answer:
Since the bottle is worth **€120**, it is above the **€75** threshold, so you need to **declare it and get your manager's approval** [1].

**What to do:**
- **Check whether the supplier is in an ongoing tender.** If it is, you cannot accept the gift, whatever its value [1].
- **Declare it in the ethics register within 5 business days** [1].
- **Get approval from your manager** [1].
- **If it is not approved**, return it or donate it to charity [1].

**Also keep in mind:**
- The €75 limit applies **per giver and per calendar year**. Other gifts from the same supplier this year count toward it [1].
- You may not accept any advantage intended to influence a business decision [3].
- The policy is owned by Compliance, applies to all employees and executive committee members, and has been in effect since 1 January 2026 [2].
items.correctness_rationale: The answer includes every key fact: the gift is over the €75 threshold, it must be declared within 5 business days and approved by the manager, it should be returned or donated if not approved, and it can't be accepted during an ongoing tender. The extra details don't contradict the reference.

items.question: What is the price per kWh of Voltaria Verte and where does its electricity come from?
items.answer:
**Voltaria Verte costs €0.2050 per kWh**, with a monthly fee of €12.90 and no commitment [2]. Its price is indexed on the regulated tariff plus 3% [2].

**Origin of the electricity:** The offer supplies 100% renewable electricity [3]. For every kWh consumed, Voltaria cancels a guarantee of origin issued by a French renewable plant [1]. The 2026 supply mix is:
- **70% hydropower** from Alpine run-of-river plants [1]
- **30% wind power** from onshore wind farms in Occitanie and Hauts-de-France [1]

Guarantees of origin are tracked in the national registry, and the yearly certificate is available in the Voltaria app [1].
items.correctness_rationale: The answer gives the price of €0.2050/kWh, the €12.90 monthly fee, and says the electricity is 100% renewable. The extra details don't contradict it, though the answer leaves out that the price includes taxes.

- **Credit:** a €300 installation credit is applied to the customer's electricity bill [1].

items.answer:

If you switch to another Voltaria offer, your price guarantee ends [1].

items.question: What happens at the end of the 36-month period of Voltaria Fixe 3 ans?
items.answer:
At the end of the 36-month period, the contract renews automatically for another 36 months at the new Fixe 3 ans price unless the customer chooses otherwise [1].

- **Two months before the end:** the customer receives an email with the new Fixe 3 ans price [1].
- **If the customer does nothing:** the contract renews for a new 36-month period at that new price [1].
- **Alternative:** the customer can choose any other Voltaria offer at no cost [1].

There is also no commitment and no termination fee, so the customer can switch supplier or offer at any time, even during the guarantee period [2]. Switching to another Voltaria offer ends the price guarantee [2].

items.question: Up to which amount can a Tier 1 agent handle a billing dispute, and what happens above it?
items.answer:
A Tier 1 agent can handle billing disputes **up to €200** [1].

- The agent checks the meter readings, the offer and price applied, and recent payments [1].

**Disputes above €200:**

**Rules for all disputes:**
- The dispute is acknowledged within **1 business day**, through the customer's preferred channel [1].
- The resolution target is **10 business days** from the date the dispute is received [1].

Goodwill gestures have a separate limit. A Tier 1 agent can grant up to **€50**, a Tier 2 team lead up to **€250**, and the billing manager anything above **€250** [2].
items.correctness_rationale: The answer says Tier 1 handles disputes up to €200 and that anything above is escalated to the Billing Expertise team (Tier 2) within 24 hours. Both match the reference, and the extra details don't contradict it.

items.question: What must an agent do when a medically dependent customer reports a power outage?
items.answer:
An outage affecting a medically dependent customer (flagged **MDC** in the CRM) is always a **P1 ticket**, and the agent must call the customer back within **30 minutes** [1].

**MDC-specific steps:**
- Treat the outage as a **P1 (critical) ticket** [1]. P1 has a first response of **30 minutes** and a resolution target of **4 hours**, both measured from ticket creation [2].
- **Call the customer back within 30 minutes** [1].
- **Escalate immediately to the DNO priority line** and **inform the shift supervisor** [1].

**Standard outage steps, which also apply:**
1. Check the DNO outage map for the customer's address [3].
2. If an outage is ongoing, give the customer the estimated restoration time and the **DNO emergency number**, available 24/7 [3].
3. Open a ticket with the category **outage**, linked to the customer account [3].
4. If there is a risk to people (fallen line, burning smell from the meter), tell the customer to stay away and call the emergency services first [3].
items.correctness_rationale: The answer covers every key fact in the reference: it is a P1 ticket, the customer gets a callback within 30 minutes, the agent escalates right away to the DNO priority line, and the shift supervisor is informed. The extra standard steps don't contradict any of it.
unsupported_claims: The standard outage steps also apply to MDC outages.

items.answer:

- **Why the DNO pays:** Voltaria Energy is an electricity supplier and does not operate the grid. Outages, network repairs and emergency interventions are handled by the DNO [2].
- **How you receive it:** Voltaria sends the claim to the DNO for the customer, and the compensation shows up on a later bill [1].
items.correctness_rationale: The answer names the DNO as the payer, gives the threshold of more than 5 hours, says the compensation is a flat rate, and says Voltaria forwards the claim for the customer. Those are all the key facts in the reference, and nothing contradicts it.

items.question: A customer is moving next month. Do they need to terminate their contract?
items.answer:
No, the customer does not need to terminate their contract. It is **transferred to the new address with the same offer, at no cost** [1]. Moving is often a case where no termination is needed [3].

What the customer and the team should do:
- **Notify Voltaria at least 7 days before** the move [1].
- **Submit a meter reading on the moving day.** This closes the account at the old address. The customer can enter it in the app, or the DNO can read it remotely [1].
- **Check that the new home has an active supply point.** If it doesn't, a commissioning request is sent to the DNO. This takes about 5 business days, and the DNO commissioning fee is passed on at cost [1].
- **Log the ticket with the category "move"** [1].

If the customer called to cancel because of the move, record the reason code **MOVE** in the CRM [3]. Then offer to transfer the contract to the new address at no cost [2].
items.correctness_rationale: The answer includes every key fact: no termination is needed, the contract moves to the new address with the same offer at no cost, Voltaria must be notified at least 7 days ahead, and a meter reading on moving day closes the old account. items.question: Can an agent paste a customer's billing data into a public AI chatbot to draft a reply to a billing dispute, and how quickly must the dispute be acknowledged?
items.answer:
**No.** Customer billing data cannot be pasted into a public AI chatbot. The dispute must be **acknowledged within 1 business day** [3].

**AI tool use**
- Customer personal data and payment data are classified as **Restricted** [2].
- Public generative-AI tools may only be used with **Public** information [1].
- Internal, Confidential and Restricted information may only be processed in the approved **Voltaria AI Workspace**. It keeps data within the EU and does not use it for model training [1].
- Restricted data must stay in approved systems [2].
- To draft the reply with AI help, the agent should use the Voltaria AI Workspace [1].

**Acknowledgement and other deadlines**
- Acknowledge the dispute within **1 business day**, by the customer's preferred channel [3].
- Disputes above €200 are P2 tickets, with a first response of **1 business day** [4].
- Service levels are measured from ticket creation. Business days are Monday to Friday, excluding French public holidays [4].
- Disputes above €200 must be escalated to the **Billing Expertise team (Tier 2) within 24 hours**, with the analysis already done [3].
- The resolution target is **10 business days** from the date the dispute is received [3].
- The final answer must tell the customer they can go to the national energy ombudsman. This applies if the dispute is still unresolved **two months** after a written complaint [5].
items.correctness_rationale: The answer says no, and it gives the reasons: billing data is Restricted, public AI tools may only be used with Public information, and the Voltaria AI Workspace is the approved internal tool. It also gives the 1-business-day acknowledgement deadline. The extra details don't contradict the reference.

items.question: Why did the team decide not to use hourly smart meter data for the first churn model?
items.answer:
The team chose monthly billing data over hourly smart meter data because of **customer consent limits**. Using hourly data would have biased the model and left many customers without a score.

**Reasoning (Data discovery workshop, 2026-03-16):**
- Karim Haddad (Data Scientist) suggested that hourly consumption patterns would be a strong signal [1].
- Thomas Girard (Data Platform Lead) pointed out that "only 41% of customers have consented to sharing hourly data", so the model would be biased towards a small part of the customer base [1].
- Nadia Benali (Retention Product Owner) added that the retention team needs a score for **every** Essentielle customer, not only those who have consented [1].

Thomas Girard had already raised the issue at the Kick-off du programme Churn & Data (2026-03-02). He said hourly meter data was "plus compliqué" because it requires customer consent [3].

**Decision:**
- Karim Haddad proposed building the first version on monthly billing and consumption data plus support tickets, and keeping hourly data for a later version [1].
- Thomas Girard agreed: "We use monthly billing data for the first model, not the hourly meter data" [1][4].

**Related later decision:** At the Revue d'architecture de la plateforme data (2026-04-21), Marc Lefèvre decided to postpone streaming of meter data to phase 2 [4].
items.correctness_rationale: The answer covers every key fact: only 41% consent, the resulting bias, Essentielle customers left without a score, the 16 March 2026 workshop, and the decision to use monthly billing/consumption data plus support tickets while keeping hourly data for later. The extra details don't contradict the reference.

items.question: What AUC did the churn model reach, and how did it evolve over the project?
items.answer:
The final churn model, a gradient boosting model, reached an **AUC of 0.82 on the holdout set**, according to Karim Haddad at the Churn model review (2026-06-02) [1].

**How the AUC changed over the project:**
- **0.74: baseline (Weekly sync 1, 2026-04-07).** Karim Haddad reported a logistic regression baseline on monthly billing, tenure and ticket counts, with an AUC of 0.74 on the validation set [3]. He explained this means the model ranks a churner above a non-churner "about three times out of four." He planned to try gradient boosting and report by Friday April 17th [3][2].
- **0.81: gradient boosting (Comité de pilotage n°1, 2026-05-12).** Karim Haddad reported that gradient boosting reached an AUC of 0.81, up from 0.74 for the first version. He named billing tickets and recent price increases as the strongest signals [4].
- **0.82: final model (Churn model review, 2026-06-02).** Karim Haddad reported an AUC of 0.82 on the holdout set, "slightly above the 0.81 we showed at the steering committee." He said the model is stable across regions [1].

**Context for the final model:**
- The four main churn drivers are [1]:
  - a price increase notified in the last three months
  - the number of billing tickets in the last six months
  - a tenure below one year
  - having no smart meter
- The pilot targets the top 10% risk decile, where precision is 0.46 [1].
items.correctness_rationale: The answer gives all three AUC milestones from the reference: the 0.74 logistic regression baseline (7 April), 0.81 for gradient boosting (12 May steering committee), and 0.82 on the holdout set (2 June review). The dates and sources all match, and nothing contradicts the reference.

items.question: What did Marc Lefèvre approve during the architecture review?
items.answer:
During the "Revue d'architecture de la plateforme data" meeting on 2026-04-21, Marc Lefèvre (CIO) approved the following [1][3]:

- **Target architecture (conditional approval):** a medallion architecture on BigQuery with dbt Core running on Cloud Run [1][3].
  - It has bronze (raw data), silver (cleaned and deduplicated) and gold (tables ready for the model and dashboards) layers [2].
  - dbt Core runs in Cloud Run jobs triggered by Cloud Scheduler [2].
  - This was chosen instead of Cloud Composer, which Léa Moreau called oversized and too expensive [2]. Thomas Girard said Composer costs "plusieurs centaines d'euros par mois rien que pour l'environnement" [2].
  - **Condition:** the CISO (RSSI) must approve the pseudonymization approach [1][3]. Under this approach, Restricted data is pseudonymized from the silver layer onward: customer IDs become hashed keys, and names, emails and phone numbers never reach gold [1].
- **Postponement of meter data streaming to phase 2** [1][3]. Hugo Lambert proposed this, noting that monthly data is enough for the model [1].

Related follow-ups from the same meeting:
- Marc Lefèvre committed to getting the RSSI's approval of the pseudonymization approach by 30 April [1].
- Léa Moreau committed to setting up the dbt project with its CI by 5 May [1].
items.correctness_rationale: The answer includes every key fact: the medallion architecture (bronze/silver/gold) on BigQuery with dbt Core in Cloud Run jobs, approved on the condition of the CISO's opinion on pseudonymisation, meter data streaming postponed to phase 2, and his commitment to get CISO validation by 30 April. Nothing in it contradicts the reference.

items.question: Quand le go-live a-t-il finalement eu lieu, et pourquoi a-t-il été décalé ?
items.answer:
Le go-live a finalement eu lieu le **22 septembre 2026**, avec une semaine de retard sur la date prévue, à cause de l'échec du test de charge de l'outil de campagne [2][3].

**Évolution de la date :**
- **Steering committee #2 (2026-07-07)** : Sophie Bernard (CFO) a décidé un go-live pour tous les clients Essentielle le 15 septembre [1]. Marc Lefèvre (CIO) l'a approuvé, sous réserve de respecter le gel estival de production du 25 juillet au 20 août [1][5].
- **Go-live readiness review (2026-09-10)** : Hugo Lambert (Engagement Manager) a décidé de reporter le go-live d'une semaine, du 15 au 22 septembre [3][5].
- **Comité de pilotage n°3 (2026-10-06)** : Hugo Lambert a confirmé que le go-live avait eu lieu le 22 septembre, et que « tout s'est bien passé depuis » [2].

**Raison du report :**
- Thomas Girard (Data Platform Lead) a annoncé que le test de charge de l'outil de campagne avait échoué la veille. Avec 14 000 clients dans le périmètre, l'outil tombait en timeout lors de la génération des listes d'appels [3].
- Léa Moreau (Data Engineer) a précisé que le pipeline de scoring fonctionnait bien, puisqu'il score toute la base Essentielle en moins de dix minutes. Le goulot d'étranglement venait uniquement de l'outil de campagne [3].
- L'éditeur disposait d'un correctif, mais Thomas Girard avait besoin de quelques jours pour l'appliquer et relancer le test [3].
- Claire Dubois (Head of Customer Operations) préférait reporter plutôt que de lancer un outil qui risquait de tomber en panne devant les agents [3].

**Actions décidées lors de cette revue :**
- Thomas Girard devait relancer le test de charge avec le correctif avant le 18 septembre [4].
- Claire Dubois devait mobiliser six agents de rétention supplémentaires pour la semaine du go-live [4].
- Nadia Benali (Retention Product Owner) devait informer l'équipe rétention le jour même [3].
items.correctness_rationale: La réponse donne le 22 septembre au lieu du 15 septembre et attribue le report à l'échec du test de charge de l'outil de campagne, qui expirait en générant les listes d'appels pour 14 000 clients. Elle précise aussi que la décision a été prise lors de la revue du 10 septembre. Tous les faits clés sont présents et aucun ne contredit la référence.

items.question: The pilot's save rate was compared with a target: what target does the retention playbook set, and was it met?

items.question: Which offer did the retention pilot target, and what is that offer's churn rate in the customer database?
items.answer:
The retention pilot targeted the **Essentielle** offer, and its churn rate in the customer database is **32.78%** (199 churned out of 607 customers) [4]. This is the highest churn rate of all five offers [4].

**Pilot target**
- At the Comité de pilotage n°1 (2026-05-12), Claire Dubois (Head of Customer Operations) proposed targeting Essentielle customers with at least two years of tenure [1].

- At Steering committee #2 (2026-07-07), Sophie Bernard decided to extend the campaign to all Essentielle customers starting September 15th [3].

| Offer | Customers | Churned | Churn rate |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Voltaria Essentielle | 607 | 199 | 32.78% |
